Reciprocal functions: the asymptotes run the show
The +c trap: inside the brackets means shift LEFT

assessmentPoints: Transformation answers in the stretch and lift activity
successCriteria: y = a·f(x) + d: stretch the height, then lift the graph: multiplying by a stretches every y-coordinate by a factor of a, and adding d lifts the whole graph by d.
y = f(bx + c): read it as f(b(x + c/b)): factor out b so the shift c/b and the squeeze by b can each be read honestly.
objectives.text: Describe stretches and translations of y = f(x), for changes both outside and inside the brackets

assessmentPoints: Asymptote answers in the reciprocal functions activity
successCriteria: Vertical asymptote x = 2; horizontal asymptote y = 1.

Take y = f(x + 3). Its root is where the inside of the brackets is zero: x + 3 = 0 gives x = -3. The original graph had its root at x = 0, and -3 is 3 units to the left of 0, so drawing f(x + 3) means taking the whole graph of f(x) and shifting it 3 units to the left - the root check settles the direction every time.
objectives.text: Sketch a reciprocal function from its asymptotes and use the root check for shifts inside the brackets

assessmentPoints: Vocabulary answers in the trap activity
Exit responses in the toolkit activity
successCriteria: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input: f(x) names the output of the rule f at the input x, and the graph of y = f(x) plots every input against its output.
A line that a curve approaches ever more closely but never touches: y = 1/x has the vertical asymptote x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote y = 0.
